title: Family offices and the licences they need
note: There is no pan-European or global register of family offices. A single family office is engineered into an exemption and never files; a licensed multi-family office files under a generic category. Only two registers name the family office directly: Luxembourg's CSSF (as a licence) and the US SEC's EDGAR (by name, for offices that must file).

licence_map.single_family_office: Outside both. AIFMD recital 7 says family-office vehicles investing private wealth without raising external capital are not AIFs; MiFID II bites only on a service provided to third parties, which serving your own family is not.
licence_map.multi_family_office: The activity is licensed, never the label: a MiFID II investment-firm authorisation for advice, order-handling or discretionary management; an AIFM authorisation to manage funds. Passportable across the EEA.

licence_map.framework: CSSF · Law of 5 Apr 1993, Art. 28-6 · Law of 21 Dec 2012
licence_map.single_family_office: A family serving only itself is out of scope and needs no authorisation.
licence_map.multi_family_office: The one European regime that licenses the thing by name: a specialised-PFS “Family Office” authorisation (€50k capital). The title itself is reserved by law to regulated professions.

licence_map.single_family_office: No authorisation where it carries on no regulated activity for others; the intra-group and “by way of business” tests keep the pure single family out.
licence_map.multi_family_office: An FCA Part 4A permission for each regulated activity it performs — managing investments, advising, arranging.

licence_map.single_family_office: A firm managing assets for a single family is generally not a financial institution — no licence.
licence_map.multi_family_office: A FinIA portfolio-manager licence (CHF 100k capital) plus ongoing supervision by a Supervisory Organisation — triggered the moment a second, unrelated family joins.

licence_map.single_family_office: Excluded from adviser registration if it advises only “family clients”, is wholly owned and controlled by the family, and does not hold itself out to the public.
licence_map.multi_family_office: Register as an investment adviser (Form ADV) with the SEC or a state.

licence_map.single_family_office: No licence if it serves one family, is not run as a business for the public, and fits the Type 9 intra-group carve-out (SFC guidance, Mar 2023).
licence_map.multi_family_office: An SFC licence for each regulated activity — typically Type 9 (asset management), Type 4 (advising on securities), Type 1 (dealing).

licence_map.single_family_office: Exempt from a Capital Markets Services licence (s99(1)(h)); from 15 Jun 2026, a class exemption that must be notified to MAS. The 13O/13U tax schemes are a separate gate.
licence_map.multi_family_office: A Capital Markets Services licence for fund management.

licence_map.framework: DIFC Family Arrangements Regulations (31 Jan 2023) · DFSA
licence_map.single_family_office: One or more connected families (USD 50m net assets per family): no DFSA licence, registered through the DIFC Family Wealth Centre and Registrar of Companies.
licence_map.multi_family_office: Serving other families by way of business needs a DFSA licence.

licence_map.single_family_office: A single family office is a “controlled activity” (family net assets ≥ USD 10m): registered with the ADGM Registration Authority, no FSRA financial-services permission.
licence_map.multi_family_office: Managing unrelated clients’ assets needs an FSRA permission.

luxembourg_cssf_family_office_pfs.source: CSSF search-entities API, specialised PFS with activity code ACT_SPP_FO

records.address: 44, avenue J. F. Kennedy L-1855 Luxembourg

united_states_edgar_13f_named_family_off.source: SEC EDGAR full-text search entity facet, Form 13F-HR filers whose name contains 'family office'
united_states_edgar_13f_named_family_off.scope: Name-based and filer-only: captures offices that manage >$100m in 13(f) securities and carry 'family office' in the registered name. Exempt and neutrally-named offices are absent by design.
